answer: Because the jetty liability is recorded in the anchor ledger at admission, the ripple audit exposes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must as a result place its own capital behind every alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. A sponsor carries 26% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. That is 25 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
